steps.caption: Open Transactions from the sidebar, under Work.
The list: each transaction's name, code, type, status, priority and current stage.
New transaction: give it a name.
Choose the type. Each type has its own stage plan — renewal starts with an existing-lease review, investment includes due diligence.
Link the confirmed requirement and the deal, so client positions and matching properties come along.
Properties under consideration, separated by commas, and the expected completion date.
More details: priority and a workflow template if you made your own.
It gets a unique code (TX-…), its type, status and current stage.

The chips jump to each of the 16 sections: overview, requirements, property, offers, negotiation, inspections, issues, stakeholders, approvals, LOI, legal, deposits, execution, possession, handover and closure.
Transaction overview: the stage plan for a relocation. The first stage is in progress; press start or mark done as work moves on.
Mark the first stage done — the next one becomes current.
Client requirements were copied from the client-confirmed requirement — only confirmed fields, nothing guessed.
Back on the list, Workflow templates let you change the stages for a type, or add a new type. Existing transactions keep their stages.
